question: Last sprint, a developer on your team asked Claude Code to replace the logging approach across your services using direct execution. Claude Code edited 30 files before the team found that the chosen approach conflicted with an existing tracing library, and most edits had to be reverted. For a similar change next sprint, what is the main reason to start in plan mode?

options.text: Plan mode lets Claude Code explore the codebase and design an approach before any files change, so conflicts surface before costly edits are made.
options.reason: The guide states that plan mode enables safe codebase exploration and design before committing to changes, which prevents costly rework like the reverted edits.

options.text: Plan mode isolates verbose discovery output in a separate context and returns only summaries, which keeps the main conversation small.
options.reason: The guide attributes isolating verbose discovery output and returning summaries to the Explore subagent, not to plan mode.

options.text: Plan mode automatically reverts all file edits whenever a test fails, so incorrect changes never remain in the codebase.
options.reason: The guide describes plan mode as exploration and design before changes are committed, not as an automatic rollback of edits after they are made.

options.text: Plan mode applies edits faster than direct execution because it skips reading files and writes all changes in one batch.
options.reason: The guide says plan mode is for exploring the codebase and designing before changes; it gives no speed benefit and does not skip reading files.
